result.title: Short-to-Long: Detached Features for Long-Horizon Value Learning
result.summary: Learning useful representations from continually changing value targets remains a challenge in deep reinforcement learning. We study the temporal horizon of this supervision: smaller discounts make these targets less sensitive to distant bootstrap changes, but using them for behavior changes the control objective. We introduce Short-to-Long (S2L), which supplies a long-horizon behavior learner with features trained by smaller-discount source networks. Detached connections prevent the behavior value loss from updating the sources, allowing each source to follow its own value objective while the behavior discount remains unchanged. Across Atari, online continuous control, and offline continuous control, the approach yields aggregate performance gains, improving the paired terminal median on 40 of 57 Atari games. Matched Atari ablations support the roles of feature transfer, smaller source discounts, and gradient isolation. Fixed-trajectory measurements further show reduced drift in source value targets with mixed discounts.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Short-to-Long：先用较小折扣的源价值网络训练特征，再通过 detached 连接把特征供长期折扣的行为学习器使用，使两者各自维持价值目标；在 Atari、在线与离线连续控制上评测，并做消融和固定轨迹的目标漂移测量。
AI.relevance_reason: 多时间尺度监督与梯度隔离的思路可能为 LVR 中多步轨迹训练、价值/信用分配与停止决策提供借鉴，但其与多模态推理的联系尚需核查。
